channel.title: The Device Layer
channel.description: An independent tech blog about security, from the metal up: hardware, firmware, protocols, and the trust decisions baked into the devices we carry.

item.title: The Architecture of Agentic Commerce
item.description: The first generation of wallets protected assets. The next generation may spend them. Software has always built more software — now software buys software, and the wallets being built for it disagree on one question: when is human intervention required?

item.title: The Psychological Signature
item.description: Why the path to clear signing isn't as clear as it seems. Before a cryptographic signature is ever produced, the user has already accepted a story — and the real attack surface is the moment that story becomes a decision.

item.title: Phishing-proof by construction: what WebAuthn gets right
item.description: Passwords and one-time codes share a fatal flaw: they can be typed into the wrong website. WebAuthn removes the flaw instead of patching it — by never giving you a secret you could surrender.

item.title: Six digits, thirty seconds: how TOTP actually works
item.description: The rotating codes in your authenticator app are about fifteen lines of code. A walk through RFC 6238: the shared secret, the HMAC, dynamic truncation — and what the design does and doesn't protect you from.

item.title: You are trusting more layers than you think
item.description: Type a password on a laptop and you've trusted the browser, the OS, the firmware, and the silicon. A field guide to the stack under your software, and how each layer fails.
